title: Spring Boot 3.5.0 to 4.1.1 on Java 21
summary: The application moved from Spring Boot 3.5.0 on Java 17 to Spring Boot 4.1.1 on Java 21. The business API is unchanged: the employee endpoints answer with the same payloads and the same authentication. Most of the mechanical change — the parent, the Java level, the test starters, the Jackson 3 packages, the actuator relocation and the mocking annotations — was made by a previewed OpenRewrite recipe; the rest was fixed by hand only where a build named it. Health and default error bodies changed shape in framework-owned fields, which is reported below rather than rounded away.

dependency_changes.reason: The parent BOM drives every managed version; set to the requested 4.1.1 by the curated recipe (section 1.1).
Java 21 is the target of this migration (section 1.2).
Boot 4 carries the MockMvc security test auto-configuration in its own starter (section 4.4).

code_changes.what: The Jackson 2 ObjectMapper bean became a Jackson 3 JsonMapper built with the same inclusion and indentation settings.
code_changes.why: Boot 4 ships Jackson 3, which relocates the databind package and replaces the mapper configuration API.

code_changes.what: Base image moved from eclipse-temurin:17-jre to eclipse-temurin:21-jre.
code_changes.why: The jar now targets Java 21 and would not start on a 17 runtime.
code_changes.evidence: Plan impact I9; no recipe changes a Dockerfile in this pack's transformation.

round_notes.diagnosis: Pre-migration reference build on Java 17: 15 tests, 2 failing actuator slice tests and 1 Testcontainers test that cannot find a Docker daemon. All three are pre-existing; the migration is judged against these counts.
Built the OpenRewrite apply immediately. Main and test code compile on JDK 21; nothing the recipe produced needed correcting at compile level.
changes: Applied rewrite-02 (curated Boot 3 to 4 recipe, previewed as rewrite-01), with ErrorResponse.java excluded as out of scope.

round_notes.diagnosis: Same package goal as round 0: the same 15 tests, the same 2 failures and the same Docker error. Nothing was introduced.

behaviour.notes: Every business endpoint is byte-identical and the authentication boundary still returns 401. The health document and the default error bodies differ in framework-owned fields only.

differences.explanation: Boot 4's health document orders details before status and adds fields; the component statuses are unchanged.
Same 401; the default error body's timestamp format changed from +00:00 to Z.

unobserved_areas: PostgreSQL-specific persistence behaviour (only H2 was exercised)

impact_review.note: UpgradeJackson_2_3 rewrote the mapper; serialization probes byte-identical.
Dockerfile edited by hand; no container runtime to run it here.

transformations.rationale: Preview inspected; applied as rewrite-02 with one file excluded.
Every changed file maps to a plan impact entry; ErrorResponse.java excluded because removing its @JsonFormat would change the error-contract timestamp.

provenance.notes: Recipe attribution per file is in transformations/rewrite-02.json.

out_of_scope_changes.change: OpenRewrite proposed removing @JsonFormat from ErrorResponse (Jackson's UseModernDateTimeSerialization).
out_of_scope_changes.why_separate: Not required by Boot 4 — the annotation still works under Jackson 3 — and it would change the error body's timestamp format. Excluded from the apply.

manual_follow_ups: Update the deployment pipeline's build image to a Java 21 JDK.
Re-run the performance suite: the runtime probes prove correctness, not throughput.
residual_risk: Only the endpoints listed in the probe file were exercised; any route not in that list is unproven.
The H2 file database was used for both runs — PostgreSQL-specific behaviour under Hibernate 7 is untested here.
